Short answer: Treat AI like a helpful stranger who can sound certain and still be wrong. Do not give it private details, and check important answers with a trusted adult or source.

What this means for your business

The goal is not a perfect blocklist. It is a repeatable family habit: pause, protect private information, verify, and talk. Shame makes kids hide mistakes; calm rules make them report one.

What to watch

  • Requests for a real name, school, address, photo, password, or private conversation.
  • Health, safety, money, or legal advice presented as certainty.
  • Generated images or voices used to trick or embarrass someone.
  • A child becoming afraid to show an adult what happened.

Do this next

  1. Write three family rules in words the child uses.
  2. Turn on the device and account controls you understand.
  3. Practice checking one surprising answer together.
  4. Create a no-punishment rule for reporting a strange message.

When Little Fight fits

This is general family guidance, not legal, medical, or mental-health advice. Little Fight can help a business set safer devices and accounts; a parent, school, platform, or qualified professional should handle a child-specific safety event.
